verdict.root_cause: cartservice cannot start because it cannot connect to its Redis backing store. At 18:52:03 UTC an automated actor (platform-automation) rewrote cartservice's Redis endpoint environment variable to point at redis-cart on port 6380 (tr_85fed96453d7). cartservice logs show the process attempting exactly that endpoint — redis-cart:6380, abortConnect off, TLS off — hanging ~20-30s per attempt and then dying with an unhandled exception thrown from the Redis store's connection-assurance/initialization path invoked directly from Main, restarting every 30-60s under a supervisor (tr_86887693af88). Because the process dies before it serves anything, cartservice emitted no call/span telemetry at all for the window (tr_91ac3e38a4fe, tr_e6243d067b7e) and every caller sees transport-level failure: frontend logs are uniformly gRPC code 14 UNAVAILABLE with connection-not-established, raised from the gRPC client library rather than application code (tr_d4562c893caf), and frontend traces show every errored path bottoming out at a CartService span, including checkoutservice's PlaceOrder inheriting its error from its own CartService/GetCart child (tr_3ac06548a0e2). The failing mechanism is the configuration value itself: the endpoint names a port the cart store is not accepting connections on, and that wrong value is what breaks every request touching the cart.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent sources converge on cartservice as the origin and on its Redis endpoint as the mechanism. Traces localise the fault precisely: catalog and recommendation spans are error-free inside the same traces whose cart siblings fail, and checkoutservice's own order-preparation work completes cleanly while its error propagates up from a CartService child span, which places the origin downstream of both frontend and checkout (tr_3ac06548a0e2). Frontend logs independently characterise the failure as transport-level — code 14, connection never established, from the gRPC client path — not a slow-but-reachable dependency and not a frontend bug (tr_d4562c893caf); the same result explicitly rules out DEADLINE_EXCEEDED and RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, and the trace evidence rules out latency by showing the errored cart spans are the fastest in the sample. cartservice's own logs then supply the mechanism: a startup-time Redis connect failure naming redis-cart:6380, in a crash loop (tr_86887693af88). The total absence of cartservice call metrics, numerator and denominator alike (tr_91ac3e38a4fe, tr_e6243d067b7e), is exactly what a process that dies before serving produces, and corroborates the crash loop rather than a degraded-but-serving instance. The change log supplies the act: a single config edit at 18:52:03 setting that endpoint to port 6380, against the conventional 6379 (tr_85fed96453d7); no deploy, no image change, no flag flip for cartservice or for frontend, checkoutservice or productcatalogservice (tr_cd5057513981, tr_b37f94d54cb5, tr_5412c29111b0), which excludes bad_deploy. Downstream symptoms fit: checkoutservice admits orders steadily but they stop completing past payment/email/write with no error line of its own (tr_24583f3db529) — a silent stall consistent with a cart call that never connects — and frontend degrades partially (~30% peak error ratio, tr_b8f9790f446f) while checkout, which touches cart on every order, degrades far harder (~0.67 peak, tr_b835f5876277). I classify this bad_config rather than dependency_latency because nothing is waiting on a slow dependency: the connection is refused/never established and the errored spans are sub-millisecond. The remediation is to restore the correct Redis endpoint value; a bare restart cannot help, since the supervisor is already restarting the container into the same wrong value.
open_questions: Whether redis-cart is genuinely listening on 6379 and 6380 is simply wrong, or whether Redis was intentionally moved to 6380 and is itself down/unreachable — no one queried the Redis backing store directly. If the latter, the correct fix is to the store, not the cartservice env var.

The prior value of the endpoint variable is recorded as absent/unknown (tr_85fed96453d7), so a literal 'revert' has no recorded target; the correct value must be established from service convention or manifests.

Timing does not fully line up. Frontend shows the identical code-14 signature at ~18:44:52, roughly seven minutes before the 18:52:03 config change, and the cartservice change result explicitly notes symptoms predating 18:52 cannot be attributed to it. Either an earlier change exists in the unqueried 18:30-18:44:45 interval (unexamined for every service), or the crash loop was preceded by a separate cart failure. This is the weakest link in the chain.

cartservice logs are truncated: healthy at ~18:44, crash-looping from ~18:57, with the 18:45-18:57 transition unobserved. The exact moment cartservice stopped serving — and whether it aligns with 18:52:03 — is not established.

No latency or saturation metrics were retrieved for any service; frontend and checkoutservice metrics are min/max summaries with no per-timestamp values, so onset curves could not be located and correlated against the change timestamp.
Why frontend peaks at only ~30% errors while cartservice is fully down is unexplained — presumably catalog-only page loads succeed, but the traffic mix was not quantified.
Whether any other service shares the same Redis endpoint configuration and was affected by the same automation run was not checked; the blast radius named 12 services and only four were investigated.
